notes: Read the complete imagined-future vignette, all thirteen candidates and the review. Preserved housing as a right asserted within the hypothetical society and linked that right to the absence of mortgage and landlord payments. Removed the invented causal relation between cost anxiety, control of time and work dread, retaining them as jointly imagined freedoms. Restored the possibility that days off would feel less urgently needed and the illustrative ordinary activities without treating them as policy guarantees.

claims.claim_text: In the imagined future without capitalism, days off might feel less urgently needed because work is enjoyable, interesting and well trained.
In that imagined future, people would pay neither mortgages nor landlords because comfortable housing is a human right.
The vignette imagines ordinary time off including school walks, errands, appointments, sport, learning, reading, travel planning, meals with others, movies and parks.
It imagines freedom to use one's time without worrying about cost or dreading a return to work.
